title: The Tidy room upstairs
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：tidy　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tidy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the gardener wrote of ① a tidy room upstairs in the notebook, and everybody in the garden said at once that it was ② tidier than the one named there the year before. Three springs on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the gardener, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the tidy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the tidiest room upstairs anybody in the garden had ever seen, or so the notebook for April 1976 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too tidy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the apprentice who had come to help; the tidy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the trowel at the far bed, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a tidy mind of the clerk, and said that no apprentice in his right mind would call it ⑥ as tidy as the mind of the clerk they had once had in the old garden. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was tidy or not, and he said so.

By 1989 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the notebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something tidy, and nothing besides. The apprentice from the next garden called the whole plan ⑧ quite tidy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the notebook kept the names of the tidy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1992, for the whole place, she wrote of another tidy room upstairs in the same notebook, and the work, which took two springs, seemed ⑨ tidier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The tidiest mind of the clerk in the whole garden, she said in 1994, was the one she could never quite name; the tidy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 整洁（前置定语 a tidy room upstairs：1982 年园丁在园艺笔记里记下的那件整洁的房间）
B. adj. 整洁／有条理（比较级 tidier than：文中两处，一处比楼上整洁的房间，一处比预想）
C. adj. 整洁／有条理（最高级 the tidiest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 整洁（表语 too tidy to do：母亲觉得它太整洁，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 有条理（前置定语 a tidy mind of the clerk：叔叔把整件事称作一桩有条理的头脑）
F. adj. 有条理（同级比较 as tidy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩职员有条理的头脑相比）
G. adj. 有条理（后置定语 something tidy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 有条理（受程度副词修饰 quite tidy：那位学徒的评价）

items.q: a tidy mind of the clerk
The tidiest mind of the clerk in

answers.why: tidy 意为“整洁”，1982 年园丁在园艺笔记里记下的是“一件整洁的房间”，此处作前置定语 a tidy room upstairs。
tidy 意为“整洁”，此处用比较级 tidier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
tidy 意为“整洁”，园艺笔记上 四月 那行字说它是园子里最整洁的一件，故用最高级 the tidiest room upstairs。
tidy 意为“整洁”，母亲认为这件东西“太整洁了，谁也用不上”，too tidy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
tidy 意为“有条理”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩有条理的头脑”，此处作前置定语 a tidy mind of the clerk。
tidy 意为“有条理”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩职员有条理的头脑一样有条理”，同级比较用 as tidy as。
tidy 意为“有条理”，园艺笔记上那半行字要的是“有条理的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something tidy。
tidy 意为“有条理”，邻园子来的那位学徒认为这套计划“相当有条理”，quite 修饰原级 tidy。
tidy 意为“有条理”，1992 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要有条理”，故用比较级 tidier than。
tidy 意为“有条理”，母亲 1994 年说的是“整个园子里最有条理的那一桩”，故用最高级 the tidiest mind of the clerk。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1982 年，园丁在园艺笔记里记下了一件整洁的房间。（a tidy room upstairs）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更整洁。（tidier than …）
母亲觉得它太整洁，谁也用不上。（too tidy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩有条理的头脑。（a tidy mind of the clerk）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩职员有条理的头脑一样有条理。（as tidy as …）
到了 1989 年，园艺笔记上只剩半行字：要的是一件有条理的东西。（something tidy）
answers: In 1982 the gardener wrote of a tidy room upstairs in the notebook.
Everybody said it was tidier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too tidy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a tidy mind of the clerk.
He said nobody would call it as tidy as the mind of the clerk they had once had.
By 1989 the notebook asked for nothing but something tidy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 tidy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1982 the gardener wrote of a tidy room upstairs in the notebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the tidiest room upstairs in the garden, or so the notebook says.
My mother thought it too tidy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a tidy mind of the clerk, and nobody argued with him.
The apprentice from the next garden called the plan quite tidy, and everybody laughed.
The tidy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
